+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""RoboPaint episode controller. Actions are generated in world coordinates."""
+import sys, math, json
+import numpy as np
+from PIL import Image
+sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/tools")
+from rcb_client import Robot
+
+Q_DOWN = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0], dtype=float)
+DT = 0.05
+
+def connect():
+    return Robot(timeout=90)
+
+def path_rows(start, waypoints, max_speed=0.10):
+    """Interpolate XYZ+quaternion waypoints at 20Hz, keeping Cartesian speed safe."""
+    rows=[]
+    p=np.array(start, dtype=float)
+    for w in waypoints:
+        q=np.array([*w[:3], *Q_DOWN], dtype=float)
+        distance=np.linalg.norm(q[:3]-p[:3])
+        n=max(1, int(math.ceil(distance/(max_speed*DT))))
+        for i in range(1,n+1):
+            rows.append(p+(q-p)*(i/n))
+        p=q
+    return np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.float32)
+
+def pose_path(r, start, waypoints, note, cameras=("canvas_cam","practice_cam","side_cam","scene_cam"), video="none"):
+    actions=path_rows(start, waypoints)
+    out=r.submit("ee_pose", actions, dt=DT, cameras=cameras, video=video, note=note)
+    print(json.dumps({"note":note,"rows":len(actions),"meta":out.meta},default=str))
+    if out.proprio is not None and len(out.proprio):
+        tip=out.proprio[-1,7:10]
+        print("tip",tip.tolist())
+    out.save("/app/runs/"+note.replace(" ","_"))

+def dip_and_test():

+    for name,img in out.last.items(): Image.fromarray(img).save(f"/app/output/cal_{name}.png")
+    print("calibration done; time left",out.meta.get("time_left_s"))
+
+if __name__=="__main__":
+    mode=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else "calibrate"
+    if mode=="calibrate": dip_and_test()

steps.text: The practice scene shows dark strokes from the test, but the overhead practice camera returned a blank frame. The arm’s reported tip reached the practice area, so I’m checking a fresh observation and camera registration before using the test to set the main-sheet strokes.

The test may have been too shallow because the arm lagged the tip targets, especially on the dip and lift. I’ll repeat one test with a longer ink dip and a slower, deeper practice stroke; that will tell us whether the apparent lines are ink marks or shadows before I commit to the main sheet.
